paragraphs: This paper studies why reinforcement learning can be inefficient when used to improve diffusion models. These models initially learn through score or flow matching, but methods such as Denoising Diffusion Policy Optimization use a differently formulated objective during reward-based training. The authors show theoretically that DDPO implicitly performs matching against noisy targets, increasing variance and slowing convergence.

Advantage Weighted Matching keeps the score or flow matching objective used in pretraining and changes how much influence each training sample receives. Samples with higher advantages receive greater influence, while lower-advantage samples are suppressed. This connects the reward signal directly to a familiar training objective instead of introducing the noisy matching targets identified in the analysis.

Across GenEval, OCR, and PickScore evaluations using Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium and FLUX, the authors report speedups of up to 34 times over Flow-GRPO without sacrificing generation quality. The result supports aligning diffusion post-training with its original learning objective; the reported maximum speedup applies to the evaluated settings.
icml-2026-advantage-weighted-matching-al.tldr: Advantage Weighted Matching makes diffusion reinforcement learning faster by weighting the original pretraining loss with reward-based advantages.

paragraphs: An LLM judging humor, dialogue quality, or role-playing can give contradictory assessments of the same response. The paper attributes this instability to dimension drift: a free-form evaluator changes the implicit criteria it considers between judgments. An explanation may therefore sound reasonable while relying on different standards from an earlier assessment.

The proposed framework makes those standards explicit through a personalized rubric. It first generates a varied collection of possible evaluation questions, then uses Expected Information Gain to choose the most informative subset. This separates constructing the evaluation criteria from applying them. The aim is to retain adaptation to the subjective task while making the questions used for scoring stable and repeatable.

Experiments on six benchmarks, including CharacterEval, The rJokes, and MT_bench, show improved consistency and agreement with human judgments compared with chain-of-thought evaluation and fixed questionnaires. These findings support selecting informative questions as a way to improve reproducibility without requiring the same static rubric for every subjective evaluation.
icml-2026-beyond-drift-stabilizing-subje.tldr: Selecting evaluation questions by expected information gain makes subjective LLM judgments more consistent and better aligned with human assessments.

paragraphs: UOJ-Bench examines whether strong programming models can also help people find and fix mistakes. Solving a programming problem and diagnosing someone else's submission are distinct abilities. The benchmark makes that distinction explicit through three tasks: generating code, finding errors through code hacking, and repairing code. It uses real submissions from Universal Online Judge and evaluates them with that platform's judging infrastructure.

The results expose a substantial gap in error detection. With one attempt, even the strongest evaluated models miss errors in more than half of a set of submissions already shown incorrect by UOJ users. Spending more computation at test time raises success rates above 90%, but the resulting inference costs constrain large-scale deployment.

The strongest models under increased test-time computation also find errors in over 5% of full-score submissions across roughly 30 problems. That finding suggests models can supply useful additional checks beyond existing judge outcomes. It does not erase the cost issue, but it identifies a practical complement to conventional programming assessment.
icml-2026-beyond-problem-solving-uoj-ben.tldr: UOJ-Bench shows that finding bugs in human submissions remains difficult for LLMs, although additional computation can uncover errors missed by online judges.

paragraphs: CalM addresses a limitation of models for neuronal calcium recordings: many are built for one analysis task and transfer poorly to others. The authors instead train a shared model using only calcium traces, aiming to learn representations that support both predicting neural population activity and decoding behavior. Pretraining draws on recordings spanning multiple animals and sessions.

Its architecture combines two components. A tokenizer converts each neuron's trace into a shared vocabulary of discrete symbols. A transformer then models dependencies across neurons and across time. Together, these components let the model represent individual activity patterns while also learning how population activity develops and how neurons relate to one another.

After pretraining, CalM outperforms strong specialized models on population dynamics forecasting. Adding a task-specific head also produces better behavior decoding results than the supervised decoding models evaluated. Linear analyses reveal interpretable functional structure in its representations. These findings support calcium-trace pretraining as a reusable basis for several neuroscience tasks, with value extending beyond prediction accuracy alone.
icml-2026-calm-a-self-supervised-foundat.tldr: CalM learns reusable representations from calcium traces that improve neural activity forecasting and behavior decoding.

paragraphs: DVPD improves speech enhancement by treating a spectrogram as both a visual pattern and a representation of audio frequencies. The paper argues that processing every region uniformly, as if the spectrogram were a generic image, overlooks useful audio structure and wastes computation. Its design uses these two views during both training and generation.

The frequency-adaptive encoder compresses different spectral regions differently, retaining important low-frequency harmonics while removing high-frequency redundancy. A lightweight visual module contributes features drawn from the spectrogram's image-like appearance. At inference time, a further refinement strategy uses the same complementary information to improve generation without additional fine-tuning. Each component contributes to using spectral structure more efficiently.

Across the evaluated benchmarks, DVPD achieves state-of-the-art performance while using 35% of the parameters and 40% of the inference multiply-accumulate operations of PGUSE, the lightweight comparison model. These results indicate that incorporating audio-specific structure alongside visual features can improve the balance between enhanced speech quality and computational requirements.
icml-2026-dual-view-predictive-diffusion.tldr: DVPD combines frequency-aware compression and visual spectrogram features to enhance speech with substantially fewer parameters and computations.

paragraphs: This paper studies how reinforcement learning policies can adapt when an environment's dynamics change. Approaches that explicitly identify physical parameters can be brittle when changes fall outside the chosen parameterization or combine several effects. The authors instead learn a representation of dynamics from trajectories, focusing on the geometry of that representation rather than requiring privileged physical information.

Their theoretical analysis connects target-domain regret to the Lipschitz smoothness of the trajectory encoder. This smoothness controls how sharply the representation can change as its input changes. They further show that optimizing a multi-positive InfoNCE objective can upper-bound the relevant Lipschitz constant, providing a training mechanism for obtaining a smooth representation that remains useful for the task.

On MuJoCo benchmarks, the method outperforms explicit identification baselines under severe dynamics changes, including unmodeled structural failures. It also improves stability within the training distribution and the interpretability of the latent representation. The findings support controlling representation smoothness as a mechanism for robust adaptation to changed dynamics.
icml-2026-dynamics-are-learned-not-told-.tldr: Learning a smooth representation of dynamics from trajectories improves policy adaptation to severe and previously unmodeled environment changes.

paragraphs: ERGeoBench evaluates how multimodal language models determine geographic location from visual surroundings. It moves beyond a single-image test by providing three increasingly interactive settings: one view, a panorama, and an embodied setting where the agent can gather observations by changing viewing direction and zoom. This makes observation gathering part of the evaluation.

The benchmark contains 2,207 street-view panoramas distributed around the world. It assesses four related abilities: basic perception, spatial awareness, commonsense reasoning, and geographic reasoning. Measuring these separately helps diagnose whether a model's localization performance accompanies strengths or weaknesses in the underlying abilities needed to interpret its surroundings.

Evaluations of proprietary and open-source models show that they can infer broad geographic meaning but struggle with detailed perception, metric localization, and maintaining spatial consistency across views. Localization performance is strongly correlated with the other measured abilities. This suggests that accurate geographic inference benefits from integrating perception, spatial reasoning, and commonsense knowledge, while the benchmark provides a way to examine those relationships.
icml-2026-ergeobench-a-comprehensive-ben.tldr: ERGeoBench tests visual geographic reasoning across static and interactive views, revealing weaknesses in detailed perception and spatial consistency.

paragraphs: FourTune targets the memory and computation required to adapt large diffusion models after pretraining. Parameter-efficient approaches reduce how many parameters are updated, but still only partly address these costs. FourTune extends low-precision computation across weights, activations, and gradients through an end-to-end four-bit training framework.

The framework adds a frozen numerical stabilizer to the usual LoRA architecture, creating a three-branch pipeline. This stabilizer isolates outlying values that are especially sensitive to quantization, helping keep training stable at four-bit precision. Block-wise quantization and customized fused kernels then support quantized backpropagation while reducing memory bandwidth overhead. The design therefore addresses both numerical stability and the hardware execution needed to realize efficiency gains.

Across customization, reinforcement learning, and distillation tasks, the authors report quality matching full-precision fine-tuning. On the 12-billion-parameter FLUX.1-dev model, FourTune reduces memory overhead by a factor of 2.25 and increases end-to-end training throughput by a factor of 2.27 relative to BF16 LoRA. These results demonstrate benefits across several forms of diffusion post-training.
icml-2026-fourtune-towards-fully-4-bit-e.tldr: FourTune enables stable four-bit diffusion post-training, reducing memory overhead and increasing throughput while matching full-precision quality in the evaluated tasks.

paragraphs: GenShield connects two tasks that are often studied separately: detecting AI-generated images and correcting visible defects in them. Detection identifies evidence of synthetic origin, while correction aims to restore a more realistic appearance. The authors develop a unified autoregressive framework in which diagnosis and restoration form a closed loop, allowing the tasks to reinforce one another.

A visual chain-of-thought curriculum teaches the model to explain its diagnosis and carry out repairs over multiple steps. An explicit stopping criterion determines when the correction process should end. This makes artifact correction a guided sequence of assessments and changes, with control over the repair process rather than an unexplained single output.

The work also contributes a large dataset pairing images containing artifacts with restored versions, together with a unified evaluation pipeline. Experiments on the new correction benchmark and established detection benchmarks report state-of-the-art performance and strong generalization. The findings support studying detection and restoration together, with explanations helping connect identified defects to the subsequent corrections.
icml-2026-genshield-unified-detection-an.tldr: GenShield combines explainable detection of AI-generated images with iterative, controllable correction of their visible artifacts.

paragraphs: Distributionally robust optimization trains against unfavorable data distributions, making the construction of those distributions central to the problem. This paper develops a gradient-flow framework for doing so. It connects Monte Carlo sampling with statistical optimal transport to turn a mathematical description of how distributions evolve into practical procedures for sampling worst-case distributions.

The framework describes this evolution using stochastic or partial differential equations. Unlike approaches centered on dual reformulations, it offers a route to algorithms for general losses, including potentially nonconvex ones. The authors instantiate the approach for a class of Wasserstein and entropy-regularized problems using Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao and Stein variational gradient flows.

Some simplified versions of the framework exactly recover previously proposed DRO methods. This gives those methods a shared interpretation and exposes insights into their theoretical limits and optimization dynamics. Numerical studies using stochastic gradient descent on machine learning tasks support the theoretical findings. The contribution is therefore both an algorithmic construction and a way to understand relationships among existing robust optimization procedures.
icml-2026-gradient-flow-sampler-based-di.tldr: A gradient-flow view of robust optimization yields worst-case distribution samplers and recovers existing methods as special cases.

paragraphs: Hyper-LLaVA addresses how a multimodal model selects relevant parameters as it learns a succession of tasks. Existing routing methods compare an input with a single center representing each task and give different modalities equal weight. The paper identifies two weaknesses: a center overlooks variation within a task, and an ambiguous modality can distort the routing decision.

The proposed router compares each sample with a task distribution in hyperbolic space, incorporating more of the task's internal diversity. It also estimates how ambiguous the task match is within each modality. Those ambiguity estimates guide adaptive balancing across modalities, reducing the influence of inputs that provide less reliable evidence for deciding which task parameters to use.

The two changes address complementary parts of routing: matching within a modality and combining evidence between modalities. The authors report large improvements over state-of-the-art approaches. The stated findings support representing task diversity and modality uncertainty together when directing a continually trained model toward the parameters relevant to an incoming input.
icml-2026-hyper-llava-hyperbolic-uncerta.tldr: Hyper-LLaVA improves continual multimodal routing by modeling task distributions and adapting each modality's influence to its uncertainty.

paragraphs: World models let agents learn from imagined trajectories, but multi-agent imagination must represent interactions without creating misleading dependencies between agents' internal states. This is particularly important for decentralized execution, where each agent acts using local information. The paper argues that existing approaches do not adequately separate individual latent states from interaction dynamics.

DMAWM divides the model into independent agent modules and a shared environment module. During real execution, each agent module forms its own latent representation from local information. The environment module is trained to reproduce this factorized structure while modeling interactions. As a result, imagined trajectories more closely reflect how information is actually available to the agents during decentralized operation.

This alignment is intended to make policies learned through imagination transfer more effectively to real-environment execution. Empirically, DMAWM achieves faster convergence and better final performance than the evaluated model-based and model-free methods. Visualizations also support its ability to capture agent interactions. The contribution connects representation structure directly to the information constraints of decentralized control.
icml-2026-learning-disentangled-multi-ag.tldr: DMAWM separates individual agent representations from shared interaction dynamics to improve learning and transfer for decentralized control.

paragraphs: LEGO tackles the cost of using language models to generate efficient GPU kernels for complete tensor computation graphs. Searching over an entire graph can be expensive, while optimizing isolated pieces can miss performance gains from combining operations. The framework organizes this search hierarchically in a recursive AND-OR FusionTree and uses multiple agents to explore alternatives in parallel.

Its two search directions serve complementary purposes. Top-down construction divides a complex graph into valid subproblems with isolated contexts, providing correctness guarantees for that decomposition and enabling independent exploration. Bottom-up mutation then attempts to fuse verified subplans, recovering global locality that separate optimization can miss. This structure prunes repetitive exploration while allowing more sophisticated combinations of operations.

Across the evaluated end-to-end models, LEGO produces speedups of 2.18 to 13.48 times over PyTorch Eager. Compared with monolithic search baselines, it reduces overall exploration time by up to a factor of 2.47 and token use by up to a factor of seven. The results combine faster generated execution with a more economical optimization process.
icml-2026-lego-an-llm-enabled-hierarchic.tldr: LEGO combines hierarchical decomposition and verified-plan fusion to generate faster GPU kernels with less search time and token use.

paragraphs: Mind Dreamer addresses a restriction in model-based reinforcement learning: imagined experience usually begins from states the agent has already observed. The authors argue that this can hold policy learning back, particularly with sparse rewards, even when the world model has discovered a broader latent structure. Their approach generates alternative starting states to explore challenging regions of that structure.

An adversarial generator proposes physically plausible latent states that expose gaps in the agent's knowledge. Because these jumps break continuity with ordinary trajectories, the method introduces relay value and uncertainty functions to carry information across the discontinuities through Bellman-style updates. Within this formulation, the authors prove that uncertainty propagation requires a squared discount factor, establishing a distinct horizon for uncertainty.

The theoretical analysis connects the method to variance-minimizing importance sampling and reduced time to reach critical bottleneck states. On the DeepMind Control Suite, Mind Dreamer reports an average speedup of 1.67 times over DreamerV3, reaching 8.8 times on sparse-reward tasks. These findings support actively choosing imagined starting points as a way to accelerate learning.
icml-2026-mind-dreamer-untethering-imagi.tldr: Mind Dreamer accelerates model-based learning by generating challenging imagined starting states and propagating value and uncertainty across latent jumps.

paragraphs: Operating-room scene graphs describe relationships among staff, instruments, and equipment using structured triplets. Existing methods can perform well overall while remaining much less accurate on uncommon relationships. SGG-ICL targets this imbalance by providing relevant examples through in-context learning, concentrating that assistance on the samples most likely to involve rare categories.

An Adaptive Router first identifies those samples and selectively sends them through the in-context learning process. Multimodal retrieval builds a pool of candidate examples, and a trained multimodal language model reranks them to select the most similar ones. The reranker learns from intersection-over-union scores computed from annotated scene-graph triplets, tying its similarity judgments to the structured relationships being predicted.

This selective strategy improves recognition of rare categories without reducing accuracy on common categories. The experiments report a 6.9% improvement in long-tail accuracy and a 2.6% improvement overall. The findings show how routing and task-informed example selection can focus additional contextual support where aggregate performance otherwise hides a substantial weakness.
icml-2026-modeling-long-tail-relations-i.tldr: SGG-ICL selectively retrieves and reranks contextual examples to improve recognition of rare operating-room relationships without degrading common-category accuracy.

paragraphs: This paper studies when multiclass partial concept classes can be learned in the Probably Approximately Correct framework. Partial concepts leave some inputs without a specified label, and the label space considered here may be infinite. The central question is which mathematical measure of class complexity correctly captures learnability across this general setting.

For finite label spaces, Natarajan dimension provides a characterization, but the authors show that it fails when the label space is unbounded. They prove that Daniely-Shalev dimension supplies the characterization for general multiclass partial concept classes. This identifies the complexity measure needed when moving beyond a fixed finite collection of possible labels.

The paper also analyzes disambiguation, which resolves the unspecified portions of partial concepts through labeling. Surprisingly, using a simple label space can destroy learnability, whereas richer labeling may preserve it. The authors characterize how the number and arrangement of disambiguation labels affect the resulting Daniely-Shalev dimension. This reveals a trade-off between label complexity and the amount of data needed for learning.
icml-2026-on-learnability-and-disambigua.tldr: Daniely-Shalev dimension characterizes general multiclass partial learnability, and simpler disambiguation labels can unexpectedly make a class unlearnable.

paragraphs: Distributional reinforcement learning predicts the full distribution of future returns. Common methods approximate that distribution with categories or quantiles, and independently sampled training targets can introduce variance while obscuring relationships between consecutive states. Path-Coupled Bellman Flows instead represents return distributions using continuous generative flows trained through flow matching.

The method connects the flow paths for consecutive states by giving them shared starting noise. This coupling creates a Bellman relation between their velocity fields, linking the geometry along the paths as well as consistency at their endpoints. A control-variate target, adjustable through a parameter called lambda, uses this structure to reduce training variance while preserving the source and Bellman endpoint geometry.

Experiments include analytically tractable Markov reward processes, OGBench, and D4RL. They show better fidelity to return distributions, more stable training, and competitive offline reinforcement learning performance. These findings support using the relationship between whole generative paths to improve distribution learning, with benefits in both the represented distributions and the training process.
icml-2026-path-coupled-bellman-flows-for.tldr: Path-Coupled Bellman Flows links generative return-distribution paths across states to reduce variance and improve distributional fidelity.

paragraphs: Video diffusion models can produce convincing individual images while generating motion that bends, stretches, or shifts inconsistently. This paper adds a physics-guided training signal to improve motion plausibility without changing the model architecture. Its central idea is to express common motion patterns through lightweight losses in the frequency domain.

The losses address translation, rotation, and scaling using global spectral cues. They act as an additional regularizer, guiding generated motion while retaining the existing video model. The method is applied to Open-Sora, MVDIT, and Hunyuan, with further evaluation on Wan 2.1-14B. Its use across these models demonstrates that the same approach can be incorporated into several video-generation backbones.

On OpenVID-1M, the authors report approximately 11% average relative improvements in motion accuracy and action recognition while maintaining visual quality. Warping error falls by 22–37%, depending on the backbone, and temporal consistency improves. Users prefer the enhanced videos in 74–83% of comparisons. Additional Wan results support gains in both video quality and physics-oriented evaluation.
icml-2026-physics-guided-motion-loss-for.tldr: Lightweight frequency-domain motion losses improve physical plausibility and temporal consistency across several video diffusion models without architectural changes.

paragraphs: LLM routers choose a model for each query by balancing predicted answer quality against cost. R2-Router questions the assumption that each model has one fixed quality and cost for a query. Output length changes both, so an expensive model might still be a useful choice if it is asked to produce a shorter answer.

The router jointly chooses the model and its output-length budget, using length-constrained instructions to enforce that choice. This expands the configurations available to the routing decision. In particular, it can identify cases where a stronger model with a shorter response outperforms a weaker model at comparable cost. The authors also introduce R2-Bench, a dataset recording model behavior across different output-length budgets.

Experiments report state-of-the-art routing performance at four to five times lower cost than existing routers. The finding supports treating response length as a decision variable alongside model identity. It shows that comparing models under adjustable output budgets can reveal useful quality-cost combinations that fixed-cost routing overlooks.
icml-2026-r2-router-a-new-paradigm-for-l.tldr: R2-Router jointly selects an LLM and response-length budget, finding stronger quality-cost combinations than routing with fixed per-model estimates.

paragraphs: CURE approaches molecular design through desired changes in cellular gene expression. This functional perspective is useful when reliable target structures are unavailable at scale or when disrupted pathways shape a phenotype. The paper formulates the task as an inverse problem: given a desired transition between transcriptomic states, generate molecules consistent with that transition.

The authors identify the problem as inherently ill-posed, with an additional gap between biological and chemical representations and sparse transcriptomic signals. Their diffusion framework uses a specialized feature extractor to summarize functional changes between pre- and post-perturbation states. It aligns those summaries with two chemical views and aggregates heterogeneous observations to extract more robust state-specific information from noisy data.

On standard benchmarks and out-of-distribution evaluations, CURE consistently outperforms strong baselines in molecular structural quality and functional consistency. A zero-shot gene-inhibitor design task provides further evidence of practical utility. These results support transcriptomic conditioning as a promising route for function-oriented molecular generation, connecting the desired cellular response to the design process.
icml-2026-reading-the-cell-designing-the.tldr: CURE generates molecules conditioned on desired gene-expression changes, improving structural quality and functional consistency in the reported evaluations.

paragraphs: Autoregressive multimodal models generate images as sequences of discrete visual tokens. A codebook connects these tokens to quantized visual patterns, making it a direct point of intervention for image safety. This paper proposes repeatedly updating that codebook using the model's own ability to understand and judge its generated images.

The first step identifies unsafe generations without human annotation and constructs corresponding harmful and safe image-text pairs. These pairs define a harmful representation space and guide codebook changes aimed at removing harmful mappings. The second step adaptively fine-tunes the codebook within the harmless space using safe pairs, with the goal of preserving the quality of generated images.

The two steps repeat until further improvement is no longer observed. The authors report iterative safety improvement without additional external feedback. The approach matters because it connects the model's judgment capability to the visual representations used for generation, while including a separate quality-preservation step. Its stopping rule is based on observed improvement in this iterative process.
icml-2026-safe-autoregressive-image-gene.tldr: A multimodal model uses its own safety judgments to iteratively revise its visual codebook while fine-tuning safe representations to preserve image quality.

paragraphs: SafeSpec combines speculative decoding with inference-time safety checks. Speculative decoding accelerates generation through a draft-and-verification process, but ordinary safety defenses can add computation or interfere with that process. SafeSpec incorporates risk estimation into verification so that checking generated content and preserving acceleration can be addressed together.

A lightweight safety head attached to the target model evaluates safety alongside semantic validity in one forward pass. When it detects an unsafe continuation, the system rolls back and uses safety-guided reflective sampling to find another continuation. The underlying model of jailbreak attacks assumes adversarial prompts increase the probability of harmful trajectories without removing safe ones, making recovery through alternative sampling possible.

Across several models and adversarial benchmarks, the authors report a better safety-efficiency trade-off. On Qwen3-32B, attack success rates fall by 15% while benign workloads retain a 2.06-times inference speedup. These results support integrating safety into speculative verification and recovering safe continuations within the decoding process, under the stated trajectory-shift model of attacks.
icml-2026-safespec-fast-and-safe-llm-via.tldr: SafeSpec embeds safety checks and recovery sampling into speculative decoding to improve resistance to attacks while retaining inference acceleration.

paragraphs: XHugWBC studies whether one whole-body control policy can work across different humanoid robot designs after a single training process. Robot-specific training limits reuse when body structure or dynamics change. The proposed framework instead trains over a broad distribution of embodiments so that the controller learns patterns shared across different humanoids.

Three components support this transfer. Physics-consistent morphological randomization supplies diverse bodies during training. Semantically aligned observation and action spaces give corresponding information and commands consistent meanings across robots. Policy architectures also model morphological and dynamical properties. Together, these components let the policy learn motion priors from varied embodiments and develop a structural bias that supports transfer to previously unseen robots.

Experiments on twelve simulated humanoids and seven physical robots demonstrate strong generalization and robustness. The reported result is that a single trained policy can transfer across a wide range of designs, including zero-shot use on unseen embodiments. This provides evidence that training diversity and consistent interfaces can reduce dependence on separate controllers trained for each robot.
icml-2026-scalable-and-general-whole-bod.tldr: XHugWBC trains one humanoid controller across varied bodies and dynamics, enabling robust transfer to previously unseen robot designs.

paragraphs: Native Network Anatomy interprets Transformer MLP sublayers directly through their weight matrices. Many interpretability methods train auxiliary models to approximate internal behavior, adding computational cost and approximation bias. This framework instead applies singular value decomposition to the existing parameters, creating a training-free route to examining their structure while retaining fidelity to the weights.

The decomposition produces orthogonal rank-one subspaces called Detector-Effector Units. Within each unit, one singular vector detects an input pattern and modulates a paired vector associated with output semantics. The authors then introduce Subspace Contribution Analysis to quantify the direct causal contribution of individual native subspaces to predictions, linking the decomposition to an assessment of functional importance.

Experiments across the GPT-2 family identify dominant functional pathways with efficiency gains of orders of magnitude over training-based interpretability baselines. The results suggest that native weight structure can provide useful, scalable interpretability information. The empirical evidence concerns the tested GPT-2 models, while the framework's contribution is the direct connection between parameter decomposition and functional analysis.
icml-2026-svd-as-a-fast-interpretability.tldr: Native Network Anatomy uses SVD of Transformer weights to identify functional subspaces without training auxiliary interpretability models.

paragraphs: Gaussian Quant offers a different route to image autoencoders that produce discrete tokens. Directly training a vector-quantized variational autoencoder is difficult because of discretization. The proposed method first trains a Gaussian VAE under suitable constraints, then converts it to a discrete model without further training. The training-free claim applies specifically to this conversion step.

For conversion, the method creates a codebook from random Gaussian noise vectors and selects the vector closest to the encoder's posterior mean. The authors prove a sufficient condition for small quantization error: the logarithm of the codebook size must exceed the Gaussian VAE's bits-back coding rate. They also propose a target divergence constraint as a practical training heuristic for making the initial model suitable for conversion.

Experiments on UNet and ViT architectures show Gaussian Quant outperforming VQGAN, FSQ, LFQ, and BSQ. The target divergence constraint also improves earlier Gaussian VAE discretization methods, including TokenBridge. These results support separating continuous-model training from discrete conversion while shaping the initial representation for that conversion.
icml-2026-training-free-vector-quantizat.tldr: Gaussian Quant converts a suitably trained Gaussian VAE into a discrete image autoencoder using a random codebook without additional training.
